identity.name: Kingdom of Kashmir
alt_names: Kashmir under the Karkota, Utpala and Lohara dynasties

land.text: Kashmir, where the Karkota dynasty is 'Preceded by: Alchon Huns; Gonanda dynasty (II)'

predecessors.note: Karkota infobox. The Gonanda dynasty (II) has no Cliopatria row and no dossier; Biswas, cited on the page, makes the founder defeat 'the last Alchon Hun ruler, Yudhisthira'.

land.text: the Kashmir Valley and its dependencies under Shah Mir: 'The Shah Miris ruled from 1339 until they were deposed by the Chak warlords and nobles in 1561'

successors.note: Cliopatria keeps this row to 1343 and starts the Sultanate in 1344; the pages put the change in 1339 (Kashmir page: 'Hindu rule in Kashmir ended in 1339 with the rise of the Shah Mir dynasty').

capitals.name: Srinagara (Srinagar)
capitals.note: Lalitaditya page: Srinagara is the old capital that stayed 'the other capital' beside Parihasapura. The pages do not date earlier capitals; Srinagara is assumed from 625.

capitals.name: Parihasapura (Parihaspur)
capitals.note: Karkota infobox: 'Capital: Parihaspur'; Lalitaditya page: 'a new capital at Parihasapura', reign c. 724/5-760, no founding year. Srinagara continued beside it.

capitals.name: Avantipura (Avantipur)
capitals.note: Utpala infobox: 'Capital: Avantipur'; no year for the move.

capitals.name: Srinagar
capitals.note: Lohara infobox: 'Capital: Srinagar'; Kashmir Sultanate infobox: Srinagar 1320-1323 and from 1339.

rulers.name: Durlabhavardhana
rulers.note: Karkota table; Kalhana's span 625-661/2.

rulers.name: Lalitaditya Muktapida
rulers.note: Lalitaditya page: modern historians date the reign c. 724/5-c. 760; Kalhana's 700-736 'is not correct'.

rulers.name: Chipyata-Jayapida
rulers.note: The Karkota table gives 832-885; the text says he was crowned in 837/8 and murdered about 840, and the Utpalas replaced the dynasty c. 855, so the strip stops at 855. The puppet rulers Ajitapida, Anangapida, Utpalapida and Sukhavarma have no dates.

rulers.name: Avantivarman
rulers.note: Utpala table.

rulers.name: Shankaravarman
rulers.note: 'died in 902 of a stray-arrow at a foreign territory'.

rulers.name: Chakravarman
rulers.note: The page also describes his death in 937; the table's 922-933 is used.

rulers.name: Partha (2nd reign)
rulers.note: Utpala table: Partha (2nd reign) 934-935 (added by the reviewer to close the gap).

rulers.name: Chakravarman (3rd reign)
rulers.note: Utpala table: Chakravarman (3rd reign) 936-937; his one-year 2nd reign in 935 is folded into Shankaravardhana's line (added by the reviewer).

rulers.name: Yashaskara-deva
rulers.note: The table gives only 939 for Shuravarman II and Yashaskara; the end is Parvagupta's accession in 948.

rulers.name: Didda
rulers.title: Queen regnant
rulers.note: The table gives 980 to 1009/1012, the text c. 980-1003 and Samgramaraja succeeded her on 8 August 1003.

rulers.name: Samgrāmarāja
rulers.note: Lohara page: 'between 1003 and June or July 1028'.

rulers.name: Harirāja
rulers.note: Reigned 22 days.

rulers.name: Ananta
rulers.note: 'In 1063, she forced Ananta to abdicate in favour of their son, Kalaśa'; Ananta died in 1081.

rulers.name: Harsa
rulers.note: Killed in 1101.

rulers.name: Uccala
rulers.note: Reigned about a decade; murdered December 1111.

rulers.name: Sussala
rulers.note: Abdicated in 1123, died 1128; Salhana (1111) and Bhikṣācara (1120-1121) were brief rivals. Reviewer: end set to 1128, when 'Jayasimha succeeded his father' (Lohara page), so the strip has no 1123-1128 gap.

rulers.name: Jayasimha
rulers.note: 'Jayasimha's rule continued until 1155, followed by his son Paramanuka'; Paramanuka's reign is not dated on the page.

rulers.name: Paramanuka
rulers.note: 'Jayasimha's rule continued until 1155, followed by his son Paramanuka, and then his grandson Vantideva (ruled 1165-72)'; years inferred from those of his neighbours (added by the reviewer).

rulers.name: Vantideva
rulers.note: 'often described as the last king of the Lohara dynasty'; Vuppadeva, Jassaka (1181) and Jagadeva (1199-1212/13) follow without full reigns.

rulers.name: Vuppadeva
rulers.note: 'Vuppadeva was succeeded in 1181 by his brother Jassaka'; start is Vantideva's end (added by the reviewer).

rulers.name: Jassaka
rulers.note: 'succeeded in 1181 by his brother Jassaka, who was then succeeded by his son Jagadeva in 1199' (added by the reviewer).

rulers.name: Jagadeva
rulers.note: 'His death came by poison in 1212 or 1213' (added by the reviewer).

rulers.name: Rajadeva
rulers.note: 'his son, Rajadeva, survived until 1235'; start is Jagadeva's death (added by the reviewer).

rulers.name: Samgrāmadeva
rulers.note: Rājadeva ruled to 1235.

rulers.name: Rāmadeva
rulers.note: Reign inferred from 'from 1252' and Laksmandadeva 'from 1273'.

rulers.name: Laksmandadeva
rulers.note: reign 'began in 1273'; 'By 1286, when Laksmandadeva's son, Simhadeva, came to the throne' (added by the reviewer).

rulers.name: Simhadeva
rulers.note: 'Simhadeva survived until 1301' (added by the reviewer).

rulers.name: Sūhadeva
rulers.note: Last Lohara ruler; infobox reign 1301-1320. Simhadeva ruled 'to 1301'; Laksmandadeva's reign (from 1273) has no end.

rulers.name: Rinchana (Sadr-ud-Din)
rulers.title: Sultan
rulers.note: Ladakhi noble who took the throne in 1320 and 'embraced Islam' in December 1320; Srinagar capital 1320-1323.

rulers.name: Udayanadeva
rulers.note: 'The rule of Udayanadeva lasted until his death in 1338'.

rulers.name: Kota Rani
rulers.title: Queen regnant
rulers.note: Succeeded Udayanadeva; Shah Mir forced her to marry him and took the throne in 1339.

ledger.note: 625: Durlabhavardhana founds the Karkota dynasty in Kashmir. Infobox 'Established: 625'; 'Kalhana assigns a regnal span of thirty-six years from 625 to 661/2'; preceded by the Alchon Huns and the Gonanda dynasty (II). The article only 'suggests' his control reached Punjab and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, from Xuanzang's visits, and that is not drawn.

ledger.note: 656: the Gilgit-Baltistan and Ladakh edge leaves the shape. Cliopatria's change; the Ladakh page has Tibet over Zhangzhung from c. 634 and the Tang-Tibet contest for Baltistan and Ladakh 'from around 660 CE'. The pages date no loss.

region.text: about 30 cells on the Northern Areas and Ladakh edge

ledger.note: c. 661: Kashmir joins the struggle for Baltistan and Ladakh. 'From around 660 CE, the Tang dynasty and the Tibetan Empire started contesting the' Tarim Basin; 'Karkota Empire and the Umayyad Caliphate too joined the contest for Xinjiang soon afterwards'; 'Baltistan and Ladakh were at the centre of these struggles.' The year is the page's 'around 660' plus 'soon afterwards'.

region.text: Baltistan and Ladakh, 'at the centre of these struggles'

ledger.note: c. 724: Lalitaditya founds Parihasapura. 'established several towns, including a new capital at Parihasapura' (Lalitaditya page); Srinagara 'continued to serve'. The page gives no founding year; the start of the reign (c. 724/5) is used.

732: the Himachal and Jammu hills leave Cliopatria's shape. The pages date no loss; Lalitaditya's war with Yashovarman of Kanyakubja is placed 'before 736' (Stein) or after it (Mishra), and Cliopatria's Kannauj-Varman row begins in 732.

region.text: about 103 cells in Himachal Pradesh and Jammu

ledger.note: c. 736: Lalitaditya makes Yashovarman of Kannauj acknowledge him. 'Kalhana describes a long war and a submission. Stein accepted the victory as historical'; Jacobi dates it 14 August 733, Stein 'before 736 CE', Mishra after 736 and before Yashovarman's death in 749-753; Mishra: 'Yashovarman acknowledged his suzerainty briefly, then became practically independent'. 736 is the bridging year of the Stein and Mishra windows.

region.text: Yashovarman of Kanyakubja (Kannauj)

ledger.note: 747: the Tang take Little Palur. 'The Tangs finally captured it in 747 CE, after three failed attempts' (Little Palur is the Gilgit Valley); Lalitaditya described himself in 733 as a Tang vassal and asked the Tang to come to Palur against Tibet, offering 200,000 troops. The Ladakh page gives no end to the struggle, so 747, the last dated event, closes it.

region.text: Baltistan and Ladakh, with Little Palur (Gilgit Valley) the last dated fighting

region.text: Ladakh and Baltistan as far as Cliopatria's shape holds them (about 130 cells)

region.text: Yashovarman of Kanyakubja (Kannauj)

region.text: the Himachal and Jammu hills added to Cliopatria's shape in 772 (about 87 cells)

1015: Mahmud of Ghazni besieges Loharkot. Siege of Lohkot page: 'Summer - Winter 1015', 'Lohkot Fort, Tosa Maidan, Kashmir', Ghaznavid Empire against the Lohara dynasty, result 'Inconclusive' (opened by the reviewer); Samgramaraja page: his advance 'was checked by the strong fort of Loharkot', besieged 'for a month' and abandoned.

region.text: the fort of Loharkot (Lohara) in the Pir Panjal, 'present-day Poonch district' (Lohara page)

region.text: the fort of Loharkot

ledger.note: 1320: Zulju's Mongols enter Kashmir. 'In 1320, a Mongol commander, Zulju, with an army of Qara'unas, entered Kashmir'; King Suhadeva 'fled to Kishtwar' and 'local chiefs asserted independence'. The army left with plunder.

region.text: the Valley, plundered by Zulju

ledger.note: 1320: Zulju leaves with his plunder. 'After committing widespread violence, Zulju left with plunder'; Rinchan then takes the throne.

region.text: the Valley

ledger.note: 1320: the Ladakhi noble Rinchan takes the throne and becomes the first Muslim ruler. 'Ladakhi prince Rinchan helped overthrow Suhadeva and took the throne in 1320' (Lohara page); he 'embraced Islam and adopted the title of Sultan Sadr'ud-Din' in December 1320 (Sultanate page). Colour and dossier continue.

1323: the Lohara line returns. The Sultanate page's infobox lists a 'Lohara interruption (1323-1339)' and Srinagar as capital 1320-1323; Udayanadeva is 'invited back' (Lohara page) and rules until his death in 1338. Colour and dossier continue.
1338: the Shah Mir-Lohara war begins. Infobox 'Shah Mir-Lohara War 1338-1339'; after Udayanadeva's death in 1338 Kota Rani rules and appoints Bhatta Bhikshana prime minister 'ignoring Shah Mir'.

region.text: the Valley, where Shah Mir revolted

ledger.note: 1339: Shah Mir takes the throne. He 'forced Kota Rani to marry him, then imprisoned her and her children and took the throne as Shamsu'd-Din Shah'.

region.text: the Valley

ledger.note: 1339: Hindu rule in Kashmir ends and the Shah Mir sultanate begins. 'Hindu rule in Kashmir ended in 1339 with the rise of the Shah Mir dynasty' (Kashmir page); 'The Shah Miris ruled from 1339 until they were deposed by the Chak warlords and nobles in 1561' (Sultanate page). Cliopatria keeps this row to 1343 and starts the Sultanate in 1344.

region.text: the Valley and its hills under the last Lohara ruler, Kota Rani, passing to Shah Mir

wars.name: Tang-Tibetan struggle for Baltistan, Ladakh and the Tarim Basin (Karkota involvement)

zones.text: Baltistan and Ladakh, 'at the centre of these struggles'

wars.outcome: The Tang took Little Palur (Gilgit Valley) in 747 'after three failed attempts'; Ladakh stayed Tibet-aligned ('may have owed its primary allegiance to Tibet'). Kashmir supplied food to Tang troops in Gilgit (722) and its king asked Tang help against Tibet (733).
wars.note: Page: 'From around 660 CE, the Tang dynasty and the Tibetan Empire started contesting the' Tarim Basin; 'Karkota Empire and the Umayyad Caliphate too joined the contest for Xinjiang soon afterwards'. Karkota page: 722 'ample food to their troops stationed in Gilgit'; 724 Princess Jincheng episode.

wars.name: Lalitaditya's campaigns (Yashovarman of Kannauj and the legendary conquests)
wars.outcome: Kalhana records a long war and Yashovarman's submission; the dates (733, before 736, after 736) and the reach of the other conquests (Gauda, Kalinga, Lata, Sindh, Punjab, the Tarim Basin) are disputed, Stein calling them 'manifestly legendary' and Huntington 'massive raiding and looting expeditions rather than true conquests'.
wars.note: Goetz dates the eastern campaign 735-736, the Lata invasion 740-746 and a Taklamakan campaign 755-756; Sen rejects the Central Asian conquest. Nothing is drawn beyond the vassal_start/vassal_end for Kannauj, at confidence 1.

wars.name: Hindu Shahi expedition of Gopalavarman
wars.outcome: 'Gopalavarman led a famed expedition against a rebel Hindu Shahi king of Udabhanda c. 903'; the spoils went to a 'Toramana-Kamaluka'. No territory changed hands on the page.

wars.name: Ghaznavid attempts on Kashmir (Siege of Lohkot)

zones.text: the fort of Loharkot in the Pir Panjal

wars.outcome: Mahmud of Ghazni failed twice at the fort of Loharkot (a month's siege, then 1021, blocked by snow) and 'did not attempt to invade Kashmir again'; Samgramaraja also sent an army under Tunga to help the Kabul Shahi Trilochanapala, who was defeated.
wars.note: The 1015 date is the label of the 'Siege of Lohkot (1015)' link on the Lohara page; the article itself did not load (pages_failed).

wars.name: Zulju's invasion of Kashmir
wars.outcome: The Qara'unas plundered the Valley and left; Suhadeva fled to Kishtwar and was overthrown by Rinchan, who took the throne in 1320.
wars.note: The Kashmir page puts it 'in about 1320'; the Sultanate page says 1320.

wars.name: Shah Mir-Lohara War
wars.outcome: Shah Mir, a councillor of Rinchan, overthrew Kota Rani and took the throne as Shamsu'd-Din Shah in 1339.
wars.note: The infobox dates the war 1338-1339; no battle is described.

certainty.note: Only the Kashmir Valley, ringed by mountains, has a natural boundary; every periphery (Jammu and Pir Panjal hills, Himachal, Poonch, Rajauri, Kishtwar, Gilgit) is approximate and mostly undated on the pages. No treaty or survey fixes any frontier.

notes:
WHAT THIS ROW IS. Cliopatria's 'Kashmir' row (626-1343, 26 shapes) is one continuous Kashmir kingdom under three dynasties (Karkota 625-855, Utpala 855-1003, Lohara 1003-1320 and the Lohara line again to 1339), not successive states: the dynasty changes are rename events here (rule 2). But Cliopatria also keeps separate rows for the Karkota (592-859), Utpala (960-1002) and Lohara (1003-1259) dynasties, drawn in different places (the Karkota shapes sit on Afghanistan, Pakistan and the Valley; the Lohara shapes run to Tajikistan), and the 'Kashmir' row itself lacks the Kashmir Valley in 626-859 and 1056-1151. Recommendation for the colour agent and the reviewer: treat karkota-dynasty, utpala-dynasty, lohara-dynasty and kashmir as ONE state (this dossier, slug kashmir, with the others' dossiers as dynasty periods); I did not edit those dossiers.
CORRECTIONS (all in keyframe_review): the Valley is added to every shape that lacks it; Xinjiang cells are dropped (no page gives Kashmir any); Ladakh and Baltistan are contested with Tibet from 661 to 747 (Ladakh page), then Tibet's (748) and Maryul's from c. 930, and are dropped from the shapes from 748; from 1294 the Xizang cells go too (Sultanate page names only the Valley as the base). The Himachal Pradesh, Jammu and Pir Panjal parts of the shapes, and the 902-959 and 1210-1227 extents, are kept as 'unverified: page budget' because no page names them; each Cliopatria jump in them has a confidence-1 gain or loss event against 'nobody' (the pages are silent on who the counterpart was). The 1236-1293 hole has a new keyframe (the 1227 outline). The state ends in 1339, not 1343.
AREA: Sultanate infobox 222,236 km2 for 1342 vs Cliopatria 201,742 (0.91); the corrected 1294-1339 outline is about 90,000 km2 (0.4 of the infobox), beyond a factor of two; see the 1294 note for the decision.
NOT DRAWN, FOR GAP-FILLERS: Durlabhavardhana's 'Kashmir, Punjab and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa' (Karkota page: inferred from Xuanzang); Lalitaditya's 733 self-description as a Tang vassal and the Tang title 'King of Kashmir' (720, Candrapida); the Mongol overlordship ('Kashmir became a Mongol dependency some time after 1235', Sultanate page; belongs in mongol-empire's and chagatai-khanate's vassal events); C. V. Vaidya's 'nominal suzerainty' of Kashmir under Harsha (Pushyabhuti page); the Alakhana territory gift under Shankaravarman (undated, unlocated); Harsa's recovery of land from feudatory dāmaras (undated). The Lohara page's own end date (infobox 1175) and the Sultanate page's start (Rinchan 1320) disagree with the 1339 used here; the Kashmir page itself ties the fall of the Lohara dynasty to 1339 in one sentence and Hindu rule to 1339 in another.
PAGES THAT WOULD NOT LOAD: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siege_of_Lohkot (error on the exact URL; the Samgramaraja page was used instead). Budget: nine pages for 26 shapes, spent as listed in sources.
STATES NEEDING DOSSIERS: Maryul (the Tibetan kingdom of Ladakh, c. 930 on), Gonanda dynasty (II) (predecessor), the Hindu Shahis of Udabhanda if turk-shahis does not cover them (Gopalavarman's c. 903 expedition), Zhangzhung. Gazetteer names used that exist: Kashmir Valley, Ladakh, Baltistan, Gilgit, Xinjiang, Xizang; the Loharkot fort is a coordinate (74.1 E, 33.8 N, 60 km) because the gazetteer lacks Poonch/Loharkot.
